from_node.description: Heidegger describes humans as challenged into ordering; one text says the human never becomes merely Bestand, while the Bremen lectures also say the human is, in a qualified way, a Bestand-Stück within ordering.

to_node.description: Heidegger therefore straightforwardly equates persons with machines or treats humans as nothing but interchangeable resources.

bridge.statement: The corpus itself distinguishes the human's participation in Bestand from machine identity and marks a special/qualified mode.

rivals.description: The apparent tension can be reconstructed as 'not mere reserve' versus 'qualified reserve-piece within ordering', not as direct contradiction.

bs4.availability: workers/operators/designers can be scheduled, allocated and functionally positioned
bs4.substitutability: organizational substitutability may apply to roles but does not exhaust personhood
bs4.demand_linkage: human labor/attention can be linked into chains of ordering
bs4.autonomy_shift: system role can dominate how the person is institutionally encountered
bs4.context_dependence: Heidegger explicitly differentiates human belonging in Gestell from machine identity
bs4.reversibility: alternative social and existential relations can interrupt or exceed resource-role description
bs4.counterdescription: labor economics, organization theory and role analysis may explain local substitutability without an ontological thesis
bs4.revision_trigger: textual evidence that collapses the qualified distinction and equates human being with machine-resource simpliciter
